'''Torsten Åkesson''' (7 November 1954), is a Swedish physicist and [[professor]] in [[Particle physics]] at [[Lund University]] who is a member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]] and was president of the [[List of presidents of the CERN Council|CERN Council]].<ref>{{cite magazine |date= 22 January 2007 |title=Torsten Torsten Åkesson takes over as President of the CERN Council |url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1010521 |magazine=CERN Bulletin |location=Geneva |publisher=CERN |access-date=23 April 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://council.web.cern.ch/en/content/presidents-and-vice-presidents-council|title=Presidents and vice presidents of Council|website=CERN Council|language=en|access-date=23 April 2017}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Åkesson graduated from Österportskolan in [[Ystad]] in 1973, and was awarded his [[Master of Science in Engineering|Master of Science in Engineering Physics]] at Lund University in 1979. He became a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] in the field of physics at Lund University in 1986 with [[Guy von Dardel]] as his supervisor with a thesis about jets.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Fysik i Lund: i tid och rum|last=|first=|publisher=Fysiska institutionen i samarbete med Gidlunds förlag|year=2016|isbn=9789178449729|editor-last=Forkman|editor-first=Bengt|location=Lund|pages=314|language=Swedish|editor-last2=Holmin Verdozzi|editor-first2=Kristina}}</ref> He continued with his research about jets in [[CERN]]. In 1996-2005 he also participated in the management team for the development of the international [[ATLAS experiment]], which among other things was one of the two LHC experiments involved in the discovery of the [[Higgs boson]] in July 2012.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://press.cern/press-releases/2012/07/cern-experiments-observe-particle-consistent-long-sought-higgs-boson|title=CERN experiments observe particle consistent with long-sought Higgs boson {{!}} Media and Press Relations|website=press.cern|language=en|access-date=2017-05-31}}</ref> Between 2005 and 2006 he was [[Chairman]] of the European Committee on Future Accelerators ([https://ecfa.web.cern.ch/ ECFA]), where he was responsible for developing a European strategy for particle physics. In 2007-2009 he was President of the [http://council.web.cern.ch/en CERN Council], where one of his main goals was to start up their [[particle accelerator]] and start the experiments at [[Large Hadron Collider]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://forska.vr.se/nummer/2007/nr12007/svenskprofessorledercern.4.47049d691193c95625a80001751.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171017203342/http://forska.vr.se/nummer/2007/nr12007/svenskprofessorledercern.4.47049d691193c95625a80001751.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=2017-10-17|title=Svensk professor leder CERN - Forska|date=2008-04-14|website=forska.vr.se|language=sv|access-date=2019-04-23}}</ref>

Åkesson is elected as a member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.kva.se/sv/om-oss/ledamoter/torsten-akesson|title=Torsten Åkesson|website=Kungliga Vetenskapsakademien|access-date=2017-05-31}}</ref> and the [[Royal Physiographic Society in Lund|Royal Physiographic Society]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fysiografen.se/en/|title=Home|website=www.fysiografen.se|language=en|access-date=2017-10-17}}</ref> and he was the head of the Particle Physics Division at Lund University during 2012–2018.

He is since 2019 co-spokesperson for the proposed experiment [https://confluence.slac.stanford.edu/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=210534721 LDMX].
